codeReview.summary: Core threshold evaluation, state tracking, transaction hooks, and subscribe-triggered initial alerts are implemented, but WebSocket authentication does not enforce the feature requirement to reject unauthenticated clients.

issues.description: Handshake auth defaults to user 1 when X-User-Id is missing or invalid (DEFAULT_USER_ID fallback at lines 21, 32, 40), so unauthenticated/invalid clients are accepted instead of rejected. This violates expected behavior 'Unauthenticated WebSocket rejected' and allows implicit access as user 1.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Shared state documents fake-auth default-user behavior for HTTP, but do not clearly define how WebSocket auth should behave under feature-level requirements that demand explicit unauthenticated rejection.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: AGENTS.md states FakeAuthFilter injects a hardcoded/default user for milestones 1-4; websocket feature expectedBehavior requires unauthenticated WebSocket rejection; implementation mirrored default-user fallback in WebSocketAuthInterceptor (lines 21, 32, 40).

summary: Review failed due to a blocking authentication gap: missing/invalid WebSocket auth headers are treated as default user 1, so unauthenticated connections are not rejected as required.
